1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Qc2 Nc6.background: Also known as the Milner-Barry Variation, after the British player Stuart Milner-Barry.

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Qc2 Nc6 5.N.strategy: Protects the d4 pawn, which the knight on c6 attacks, and develops a piece. White keeps its set-up flexible and waits to see how Black builds its centre, with the unpinning of the knight still in reserve.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Qc2 Nc6 5.N.name: Nimzo-Indian Defence: Classical Variation, Zurich Variation

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Qc2 Nc6 5.N.strategy: The idea of the variation: Black prepares a pawn centre on d6 and e5, which leaves the light-squared bishop free on its diagonal. Black has accepted giving up the dark-squared bishop in return for a flexible, solid structure.
Castles first and keeps the choice of pawn structure open. It delays the central pawn plan, which can be prepared with a rook or the queen, but gives White time to unpin the knight.
